themes.label: Praise: accurate period tracking
themes.summary: Most reviewers in this cluster are praising Flo for accurate cycle and ovulation predictions, daily insights, and long-term use across periods and pregnancies. A minority say the value is undercut by paywalls, with core info like symptom guidance, late-period explanations, and health assistant messages locked behind premium, and some find the constant subscription prompts pushy.
themes.recommendation: Protect the prediction accuracy and pregnancy mode that drive praise, and audit which free-tier features (symptom expectations, late-period explanations) are gated, so the team can decide whether to move a few high-value items to free and tighten how often the Flo bot prompts non-subscribers to upgrade.

themes.label: Excessive premium upsell pop-ups
themes.summary: Users across iOS and Android say the app opens with or repeatedly shows full-screen pop-ups and ads pushing Premium, often requiring several taps to exit before they can reach their period calendar or logs. Many feel the upsell has grown over successive versions, with some saying they have stopped using the app or plan to switch, despite years of stored data that makes leaving costly.
themes.recommendation: Audit the paywall trigger frequency across app entry, calendar, and notification flows, then test a version that caps upsell prompts per session with a visible close button and a snooze or opt-out setting, measuring retention and uninstall rates against the current build.

themes.label: Login and data loss on new phone
themes.summary: Android users switching to a new device report being unable to log in to their existing account, with password reset emails never arriving and the app either creating an empty new profile or showing errors instead of restoring their history. Many say they were forced through long onboarding questionnaires and subscription pitches before reaching the login button, and support replies are described as automated and unhelpful, leading several to cancel.
themes.recommendation: Investigate the Android device-change login flow end to end: reproduce a sign-in on a fresh device with an existing email account, check password reset email delivery logs for Android-initiated resets, and make the login option reachable before onboarding so returning users can restore data without going through the questionnaire.

themes.label: Unwanted charges after cancellation
themes.summary: Users across iOS and Android report being charged for Flo premium or annual subscriptions after cancelling, or after signing up for a free trial that charged immediately. Many say cancellation is hard to complete because the in-app option is missing, the website fails to load, or support does not respond, and refunds are often denied. The cluster is consistent in theme, with recurring references to free trial conversions and charges appearing months after users uninstalled the app.
themes.recommendation: Audit billing for cancelled and trial-converted subscriptions over the last 12 months, including charges routed through the web and Apple/Google billing, and ship an in-app cancellation path that also stops renewals on the web checkout and sends a confirmation email.

themes.label: Core features locked behind paywall
themes.summary: Users across Android and iOS feel the free tier only offers basic tracking or a calendar, while tips, insights, and information like pregnancy or period questions require a subscription, which many find too expensive or inaccessible, especially teenagers and people with limited income. Several reviewers say the app previously was free or better value and that constant upgrade prompts and ads make the experience feel like a money grab.
themes.recommendation: Audit which currently paywalled educational content (insights, tips, FAQ answers) could move to the free tier or a lower-priced plan, and run a pricing test measuring retention and conversion for a cheaper annual option or student/low-income pricing.

themes.label: Core features locked behind paywall
themes.summary: Users across iOS and Android say basic tracking works, but most educational content, insights, and features like symptom interpretation, pregnancy details, and chat require a premium subscription that many felt was dropped on them after a long onboarding questionnaire. Several say the app was previously free or that they were promised free access, and teens and people without money feel especially shut out. Some reviewers mention they are uninstalling or switching to free alternatives.
themes.recommendation: Audit the free tier against the paywall: list which educational and insight features (cycle phases, discharge guide, late-period info, pregnancy week updates) are gated, then test moving a defined set into free and add a free trial or preview before the paywall appears at the end of onboarding.

themes.label: Core health content locked behind paywall
themes.summary: Users across Android and iOS say the app is useful for period tracking but that educational articles, advice on topics like discharge, acne and sex, and even basic information are gated behind a subscription, which many find unfair given the subject matter. Several reviewers, including teens and users who cannot afford premium, feel basic women's health education should be free, and some describe frequent subscription pop-ups.
themes.recommendation: Audit which articles and advice currently sit behind the paywall, identify a core set of basic health education to move to the free tier, and A/B test the subscription prompt frequency to measure its effect on ratings and retention.

themes.label: Praise for cycle tracking accuracy
themes.summary: Most reviews in this cluster are enthusiastic praise for Flo as a reliable period and cycle tracker, with users citing accurate predictions, ease of use, and helpful pregnancy tracking. A recurring complaint sits alongside the praise: several users say useful articles, tips, and assistant answers are now locked behind premium, and some felt the free tier was reduced over time. Reviews come from both Android and iOS across many app versions.
themes.recommendation: Protect the core prediction and logging experience while running an analysis of which free-tier content (articles, cycle tips, assistant answers) was moved behind premium in recent versions, then decide which items to restore to free to reduce paywall frustration.

themes.label: Praise: cycle tracking and insights
themes.summary: Users overwhelmingly praise Flo for accurate period and ovulation predictions, easy symptom logging, and useful health education across pregnancy, body changes, and sexual health. A few reviews add requests such as more contraception types (implants, IUDs) in the log, custom symptom tags, and tracking gas, leg pain, and blood pressure. One user who had a bilateral salpingectomy and another who recently had a baby say pregnancy content dominates their home screen or daily feed even after switching modes or updating.
themes.recommendation: Protect the prediction accuracy and logging ease that drive praise, and scope a ticket to let users with non-pregnancy goals (post-tubal ligation, post-partum or post-loss) fully hide or replace pregnancy and baby-related cards and daily content, starting with a survey of which contraception methods and custom symptoms to add to the log.

themes.label: Praise: cycle tracking, with paywall complaints
themes.summary: Most reviews in this French-language cluster praise Flo for cycle tracking, symptom logging, reminders, and period predictions, and many call it the best app of its kind. The lower-rated reviews focus on aggressive Premium upsells that appear on every app open, features locked behind the subscription, and a charge plus hard-to-find cancellation (web-only) that one user says they did not authorize. A few users also say the app lacks endometriosis-related symptom options and post-pregnancy or breastfeeding cycle guidance.
themes.recommendation: Audit the Premium upsell frequency and placement for iOS users in French-speaking markets, and review the subscription cancellation path and any web-to-App Store billing handoff for clarity and consistency, then ticket fixes for the unauthorized-charge and cancellation complaints first.

reviews.t: Good intentions, not executed so well.
reviews.x: While I think this app has good intentions, it doesn’t always execute it well. -Forums seem at first like a good idea, but they don’t always work out. In sections where younger people who got their periods more recently are talking, a lot of misinformation is being spread, which I believe could have a long term impact on someone reading. The problem is that the people giving answers are just as clueless as those seeking them. -This app is very gendered. It constantly talks about people who have periods as ‘girls’ or ‘women’. They ignore the fact that not everyone who gets a period is a women, and standards like that can cause a lot of hurt to those who get periods but do not identify as female. Otherwise, it’s an alright app for tracking periods. I just found it very hard to use because the amount of misinformation spread through this app bothered me. I feel like just a period tracker would have been enough.
